newsitem.title: USA: Toro says Q3 to be below expectations.
newsitem.headline: Toro says Q3 to be below expectations.

text.p: Toro Co said Tuesday that third-quarter earnings, before an extraordinary charge related to debt restructuring, will be well above last year's third quarter, but below analysts' expectations.
"This difference will be offset by fourth quarter earnings which should be above market expectations," Toro said.
"Earnings for the full year are on target to meet analyst expectations and should provide another record performance for the company," said the lawnmower manufacturer.
The company said, "Weather and changing market conditions are causing Toro's third and fourth quarter performances to differ from original plans."

Chief executive Kendrick Melrose said, "Weather clearly shortened the spring and summer selling season for consumer mowing products, with floods and drought stagnating the lawn and garden industry worldwide ... Moreover, dealers continued their conservative ordering trend which affects the delicate balance between shipments, retail sales and field inventory levels. We are committed to keeping field inventory levels low and to accommodate this goal we reduced shipments."

He added, "As we saw these situations develop during the quarter, we initiated proactive cost containment efforts which offset these issues and should enable us to leverage sales and meet our earnings target for the year."

A one-time call premium charge relating to the redemption of $50 million of outstanding 11 percent sinking fund debentures, announced earlier in the quarter, will reduce earnings as an extraordinary item, Toro said.
The company could not immediately be reached for further comment.

The First Call consensus estimate for third-quarter Toro earnings is $0.83 per share, versus $0.52 per share a year ago. The fiscal 1997 consensus earnings estimate is $2.99 per share, versus $2.90 per share, First Call said.
